cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic Hawaiian ʻuliʻuli hula rattle — a gourd handle topped with a feather-covered disc arrangement with a central shell — a traditional Native Hawaiian dance instrument, matching both the claimed ethnicity and category.

physical.title: dance-rattle
physical.summary:
Registration slip description by C H Read written in 1895:
Hula rattle (uliuli hula) consisting of a small gourd containing seeds, from which issues a bouquet-shaped framework of sticks and dried palm-leaves. The upper surface of this framework is concave and circular, and is ornamented with two concentric circles of cocks' feathers alternating with two circles of [iiwi] red feathers etc. The centre is ornamented with a shell disc.

physical.title: drum
physical.summary:
Register slip description by C H Read, written in 1895:
Small drum consisting of half a coconut of pale colour, one side of which is split, resting on the upper end of a hollow cylinder of palm wood with six oblong apertures round the base, one of which is imperfect. A pale membrane covers the coconut, and is strained by cords of twisted sinnet secured through the apertures in the palm wood cylinder below.
